models._description: Adds action_privacy_lookup launcher from a partner form

behavioral_notes.observation: The discovery engine. action_lookup() builds one raw SQL UNION ALL query (_get_query) and runs it via cr.execute, then materialises every matched row as a privacy.lookup.wizard.line (res_model_id, res_id, is_active). The query has three layers: (1) an indirect_references CTE of res_partner rows whose email_normalized equals, or name ilike, the subject; (2) explicit UNIONs over res_partner, res_users (matched by login or by partner_id), and mail_message (author_id in the CTE, to catch direct-message authorship); (3) a dynamic sweep across EVERY non-transient, non-abstract model in self.env. The cross-model UNION is the metadata-invisible core: the wizard does NOT have a fixed list of 'personal data' tables — it derives them at runtime.

How it decides which models hold personal data, per model in self.env (minus a blacklist of res.partner/res.users/mail.notification/mail.followers/discuss.channel.member/mail.message): (3.1) DIRECT match — if the model has any stored field named email_normalized/email/email_from/company_email it adds an email condition (exact '=' on normalised columns, else ilike on the full 'Foo Bar <foo@bar.com>' string) and, when the model's _rec_name is a stored non-translated char, also an ilike on the name; (3.2) INDIRECT match — for every stored many2one field whose comodel is res.partner with ondelete != 'cascade', it adds `<fk> IN (SELECT id FROM indirect_references)`. Cascade FKs are skipped because deleting the partner already removes them. Each matching model contributes another UNION ALL branch carrying its ir.model id, row id and active flag.

Erasure is applied per matched record, not by a single global action. _onchange_is_active() writes active=True/False (archive/unarchive) on env[res_model].sudo().browse(res_id) and records 'Archived/Unarchived <Model> #id' into execution_details. action_unlink() calls .sudo().unlink() on the target record, sets is_unlinked=True and records 'Deleted <Model> #id'. action_archive_all/action_unlink_all iterate the lines to bulk-apply. Every action runs sudo() so it can reach records the privacy officer might not otherwise write/delete. No actual scrubbing of res.partner happens here — anonymisation of the subject's own identity is left to the audit log (see next note).

privacy.log is the immutable GDPR audit record, created automatically by wizard._post_log() when execution_details exist (compute side-effect of _compute_execution_details). Its create() override masks the subject's identity before storage: _anonymize_name turns 'John Doe' into 'J*** D**', _anonymize_email turns 'john.doe@example.com' into 'j***.d**@e******.com' while preserving common public domains (gmail.com/hotmail.com/yahoo.com) and the TLD. So the log proves WHAT was erased and by WHOM (user_id, date, records_description) without itself re-storing the personal data — the masking is in code, not visible from field metadata.

Static UI only, no OWL/JS (frontend.present=false). The wizard is reached two ways: a 'Privacy' menu under Settings (base.menu_custom) exposing read-only Privacy Logs (list+form, create:False), and a res.partner.action_privacy_lookup button that opens the wizard pre-filled with the partner's email/name. Lines render via a generic ir.model Reference widget (resource_ref) so any matched record is clickable. All access (ir.model.access.csv) is restricted to base.group_system — only the System administrator can run a lookup or erase records.

logical_data_erm: privacy.lookup.wizard.line -> * (resource_ref dynamic Reference to any matched record)
information_flows: lookup: partner.action_privacy_lookup / wizard -> _get_query (dynamic SQL UNION over all models) -> cr.execute -> privacy.lookup.wizard.line per matched record
erasure: wizard.line.action_unlink/_onchange_is_active -> sudo().unlink()/write(active) on env[res_model].browse(res_id) across arbitrary business models
audit: wizard._post_log -> privacy.log.create (anonymises subject name/email, captures execution_details + records_description + user_id)
discovery scope: every non-transient stored model with an email-like field or a non-cascade many2one->res.partner is swept (heuristic, not a fixed registry)

capabilities: Data-Subject Access / Lookup (find every record tied to a person across all models)
Right-to-Erasure Execution (archive or delete matched records)
Personal-Data Discovery (heuristic detection of which models hold PII)
Privacy Audit Logging (tamper-resistant, identity-masked record of erasures)
value_streams: Request-to-Erasure: data-subject request -> lookup (build cross-model match set) -> review lines -> archive/unlink records -> masked privacy.log audit entry
Lookup-to-Disclosure: partner -> action_privacy_lookup -> enumerated matched records (subject-access support)
organization: base.group_system (System administrator — sole holder of all privacy_lookup access)
policies: Access to lookup/erasure and to Privacy Logs restricted to base.group_system
Privacy Logs are read-only in the UI (create:False) — append-only audit trail
privacy.log.create() masks subject name/email before persistence (data-minimisation)
Discovery skips cascade-delete FKs and a blacklist of mail/discuss link models to avoid double-handling
Erasure runs as sudo() to reach records the operator may not directly own
stakeholders: Data Protection Officer / privacy team (runs lookups and erasures)
Data subject (person whose records are looked up / erased)
Regulator / auditor (consumer of the privacy.log audit trail)
metrics: Count of records matched per model (records_description)
Erasure execution log volume (privacy.log entries over time)

classification.rationale: privacy_lookup is a compliance / data-governance utility with no business object of its own — its only models (privacy.log + two transient wizard models) exist to operate ON other modules' data, sweeping every model for a person's PII and then archiving/deleting it. This is a classic Porter/Stabell-Fjeldstad 'support' activity: a firm-level risk/IT governance function, not a value-creating primary chain/shop/network step (there is no product, no customer-facing transaction, no document chain it owns). auto_install=true and access gated to base.group_system confirm it is internal administrative tooling. APQC 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' is chosen because the module operationalises a data-privacy governance capability — defining and enforcing how personal data is discovered, retained and erased across the enterprise's information assets (the 'manage knowledge/information governance' strand of 13.0). 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation, and Resiliency' was a close alternative (GDPR is a regulatory-compliance obligation and erasure is a compliance-remediation act); it is a defensible mapping. 13.0 is preferred here because the tool's substance is governance of the data/information capability itself (PII discovery + lifecycle/erasure across all data objects) rather than the broader risk-register/control-testing scope that 11.0 centres on — the module manages a capability over enterprise information, with compliance as the driver.

standard_capabilities: Cross-model personal-data lookup by name + email (heuristic over all stored models)
Per-record archive / unlink and bulk archive-all / unlink-all erasure
Launch from a partner form (action_privacy_lookup) or the Settings > Privacy menu
typical_fits: Handling a GDPR data-subject access or erasure request for a known partner/email
Demonstrating an auditable erasure trail to a regulator (privacy.log)
common_gaps: Pseudonymisation/scrubbing of field values in place is not offered — only archive or full unlink (records are removed, not redacted-but-kept)
Discovery is heuristic: models without an email-like field and without a non-cascade many2one to res.partner are invisible (free-text PII, custom link models, JSON blobs are missed)
No workflow / approval / SLA tracking around the request (single admin wizard run)
No automatic consent or retention-policy enforcement; erasure is manual and operator-driven
unlink() may fail on records protected by ORM constraints / referential integrity (not surfaced as a managed exception path)
drive_hints: odoo shell: w = env['privacy.lookup.wizard'].create({'name':'John Doe','email':'john@example.com'}); w.action_lookup(); w.line_ids.mapped('res_model')  # see which models matched
odoo shell: print(env['privacy.lookup.wizard'].new({'name':'A','email':'a@b.com'})._get_query())  # inspect the generated discovery SQL
UI: open a res.partner form > Action > Privacy Lookup, then archive/delete matched lines and check Settings > Privacy > Privacy Logs

open_questions: Real-world recall of the heuristic: what fraction of PII-bearing custom models lack both an email-like field and a non-cascade partner FK (and are therefore missed)?
Whether downstream modules add their own privacy hooks/overrides to extend the sweep (none observed in this module).
Behaviour and failure handling when unlink() hits referential-integrity or access constraints on a matched record.
